report.summary: Knorr-Bremse AG is a Munich-headquartered global leader in rail and commercial vehicle brake systems. The company presents an elevated supplier-risk profile driven by repeated 2024-2025 NHTSA safety recalls of brake chambers and a resolved 2018 U.S. Department of Justice antitrust settlement over no-poach agreements with Wabtec. Additional considerations include a European Commission merger investigation into the proposed Haldex acquisition, historical forced-labor use during the Third Reich, and criticism of Russia sanctions. Procurement buyers should prioritize product-safety verification, recall remediation status, and antitrust compliance before engagement.

facts.text: The U.S. Department of Justice announced a settlement with Knorr-Bremse AG and Westinghouse on April 3, 2018, concerning no-poach agreements in violation of Section 1 of the Sherman Act.
The European Commission opened merger investigation Case M.8222 into Knorr-Bremse's proposed acquisition of Haldex, involving horizontal overlaps in commercial vehicle brake systems and components.
NHTSA Safety Recall Report 24V-559 involves Knorr-Bremse brake chambers on Nova Bus vehicles with production dates July 6, 2020 - June 3, 2021, due to a potential manufacturing defect.

Bendix is recalling approximately 1,672 Knorr-Bremse 22/24-57 brake chambers, part number K068622, sold as replacement parts for certain buses, due to improper manufacturing that can result in an air leak.
NHTSA Part 573 Safety Recall Report 25E048 references Knorr-Bremse-related addresses and component involvement, indicating a 2025 safety recall affecting Knorr-Bremse brake chambers.
NHTSA Part 573 Safety Recall Report 25E-027 concerns brake chamber seal design with no warning prior to occurrence, involving Knorr-Bremse components.

Knorr-Bremse's company history discloses that at the Berlin parent plant, the number of foreigners employed reached a wartime peak of 3,101 (42.3% of the workforce of 7,334) during the Third Reich period 1933-1945.
